extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys facing USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing imposition of reciprocal discipline (exclusion) by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on disciplinary action in another jurisdiction, including service, notice, opportunity to respond, and required post-order publications/notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline based on a disciplinary order from another jurisdiction (here, disbarment on consent by the North Carolina State Bar) pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline mirrors the discipline imposed by the other jurisdiction unless the respondent establishes one of the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1) to oppose imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical violations triggering exclusion (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a),(b) via 10.23(c)(5)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5)(i) (for example, misappropriation of entrusted client funds) can support exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites misappropriation of entrusted client funds from a trust account as the basis for the underlying disbarment that supports reciprocal exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order to respondent (mailing to last known address)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order initiating reciprocal discipline must be mailed (certified mail) to the respondent at the last address known to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents mailing by certified mail (with receipt number) to the respondent's last known address and that the Notice informed respondent of the Complaint and the opportunity to respond within 40 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate service by publication when mailing is undeliverable (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Notice and Order cannot be served at the respondent's last known address (e.g., returned 'Unclaimed'), service may be effected by publication in the Official Gazette pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice was published in the Official Gazette on specified dates and the publication informed the respondent how to request copies of the Notice and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity and timeframe to respond (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for determination when respondent does not respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Director may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that exclusion from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states that in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact and (2) exclusion is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and effective date of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: When ordered, the respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies exclusion covers patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO and takes effect as of the Final Order's date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of Official Gazette notice of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the respondent (name and registration number), state the reciprocal discipline imposed, cite the regulatory provisions violated (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(5)(i)), and describe the basis (e.g., disbarment on consent for misappropriation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes a model notice text stating respondent's name, registration number, that exclusion is ordered for violating specified regs by being disbarred on consent, and a factual sentence about misappropriation of entrusted client funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-order notification requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to notify state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public and to publish the notice in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references the Reading Room URL where decisions are available for public reading and directs publication of the notice there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory basis for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (and related provisions cited in the Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly states it is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 and cites regulatory sections for service, opposition, notification, and scope of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for additional relief as necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order contemplates directing such other and further relief as the nature of the cause shall require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides discretionary authority to require additional remedial measures beyond exclusion and notices if warranted by the circumstances.
